article.headline: Google Drive's Scanner Quietly Grows Up With Serious Features
article.lede: Google has been quietly upgrading the document scanner embedded in Google Drive, and a cluster of new capabilities — demonstrated in a viral clip — suggests the company is making a serious play for the mobile scanning workflow. The update bundles features that until recently distinguished dedicated scanning apps from the bundled, good-enough alternatives. For millions of users who already live inside Google's productivity suite, the gap just narrowed.
article.body:
The headline additions are *continuous capture* and real-time multi-page scanning. Traditional mobile scanners — including earlier versions of Drive's own tool — require the user to tap a shutter for each page, wait for processing, then proceed. Auto-capture removes that friction: the app detects a document in frame, locks on it, and advances automatically, compressing a ten-page scan into a fluid, uninterrupted motion. That workflow has been a selling point for Adobe Scan and Microsoft Lens for years.

**Duplicate page detection** is the subtler addition, and arguably the more practically useful one. Anyone who has scanned a thick document while distracted knows the problem: you get home, open the PDF, and find page seven twice. Catching that redundancy in real time — rather than after the fact in editing — removes a persistent annoyance that has never quite been glamorous enough to headline a product launch.

The redesigned beta interface signals that these are not minor patches bolted onto old scaffolding; Google appears to be rebuilding the scanner as a first-class surface. That matters because Drive is the default storage layer for a vast portion of Android devices and Google Workspace subscribers. A scanner that ships pre-installed and now performs comparably to dedicated apps is a meaningful distribution advantage — one that erodes the use case for downloading a separate scanning app at all.

The caveat is that 'beta' carries real weight here. Features shown in preview clips have a way of shipping with rough edges, delayed rollouts, or narrower device support than the demos imply. Whether continuous capture works reliably under imperfect lighting — the condition under which people most often need to scan — will determine whether this upgrade genuinely changes behavior or simply looks impressive on a phone held at the right angle.

concepts.definition: A scanning mode in which the app automatically detects and photographs each document page without requiring a manual shutter tap between pages. The camera stays live, advancing the scan as soon as a new page is positioned in frame, dramatically reducing the time and attention needed to digitize multi-page documents.

An automated check that identifies when the same page has been captured more than once during a scanning session. Rather than requiring the user to review and delete duplicates in post-processing, the scanner flags or discards the redundant image in real time.

ticker_googl.name: Alphabet Inc. (Class A)
ticker_googl.blurb: Alphabet is the parent company of Google, the world's dominant search engine, as well as YouTube, the Google Cloud Platform, and a portfolio of moonshot bets (Waymo, DeepMind, Verily). Search advertising accounts for the majority of revenue, but the cloud division has grown into a multi-billion-dollar profit centre. Alphabet is also a leading player in generative AI, having developed the Gemini family of large language models and integrated them across its product suite.
ticker_googl.recent: Alphabet reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $370 billion, with Google Cloud crossing $50 billion annually. The company has faced antitrust scrutiny in both the US and EU, with a US federal court ruling in 2024 that Google holds an illegal monopoly in general search. Despite regulatory headwinds, the stock has benefited from AI-driven search enhancements and strong cloud growth.
